U-shaped patterns in income growth

Use sample_growth_tb to examine the ratio of log growth over the first three years to log growth over the full six years for individuals whose 2014–2020 log growth exceeds a threshold. Examine whether the ratio exhibits a U-shape concentrated near zero and one, as predicted by subexponentiality.

1 Data preparation and ratio construction

library(tidyverse)
library(pins)
# Specify relative paths for the board, figure output directory, and plotting theme.
board <- board_folder("../income_board_replicate")
graph_dir <- "graph"
dir.create(graph_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
source("theme_ipsum_like.R")
theme_set(theme_ipsum())

Definition of the ratio variable

Load sample_growth_tb and calculate age age as the beginning year extracted from the period label minus the birth year in the first four characters of birth_date. For records in each period, select observations with beginning-of-period income of at least 4 million yen and beginning-of-period age 25–60, then reshape growth rates to wide format by ID. Both periods used in the ratio, 2014–2017 (g_17_14) and 2014–2020 (g_20_14), start in 2014, so the same 2014 income and age conditions apply to both. Retain observations with finite growth rates in both periods in ratio_tb. Define the ratio as \(r_{20,14}=g_{17,14}/g_{20,14}\).

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year,6,7))) - as.numeric(str_sub(birth_date, 1, 4))) |> 
  filter(pre_income >= 4*10^6, 
         age >= 25, age <= 60)

ratio_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = growth) |>  
  filter(is.finite(g_17_14), is.finite(g_20_14)) |>
  mutate(r_20_14 = g_17_14 / g_20_14)

2 Ratio distributions by threshold

Share of growth occurring in the first three years

Exclude observations with ratios exactly equal to zero or one, and set 28 threshold values \(u\) from 0.1 to 2.8 in increments of 0.1. For each threshold, select individuals whose six-year growth satisfies \(g_{20,14}>u\). Restrict the horizontal axis to −0.3–1.3 using xlim().

x_values <- seq(0.1, 2.8, by = 0.1)

plot_tb <- ratio_tb |>
  select(id, r_20_14, g_20_14) |>
  filter(r_20_14 != 0, r_20_14 != 1)

plots <- map(x_values, \(threshold) {
  plot_tb |>
    filter(g_20_14 > threshold) |>
    ggplot(aes(r_20_14)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
    xlim(c(-0.3, 1.3)) +
    ggtitle(paste("u =", threshold)) +
    labs(x = "Ratio", y = "Frequency")
})

walk(plots, print)
walk2(plots, x_values, \(plot, threshold) {
  ggsave(
    filename = str_c("ratio_three_x_", threshold, "_income.png"),
    path = graph_dir,
    plot = plot
  )
})

Use `sample_growth_tb` to examine the ratio of log growth over the first three years to log growth over the full six years for individuals whose 2014–2020 log growth exceeds a threshold.
Examine whether the ratio exhibits a U-shape concentrated near zero and one, as predicted by subexponentiality.

## 1 Data preparation and ratio construction

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)
# Specify relative paths for the board, figure output directory, and plotting theme.
board <- board_folder("../income_board_replicate")
graph_dir <- "graph"
dir.create(graph_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
source("theme_ipsum_like.R")
theme_set(theme_ipsum())

```

**Definition of the ratio variable**

Load `sample_growth_tb` and calculate age `age` as the beginning year extracted from the period label minus the birth year in the first four characters of `birth_date`.
For records in each period, select observations with beginning-of-period income of at least 4 million yen and beginning-of-period age 25–60, then reshape growth rates to wide format by ID.
Both periods used in the ratio, 2014–2017 (`g_17_14`) and 2014–2020 (`g_20_14`), start in 2014, so the same 2014 income and age conditions apply to both.
Retain observations with finite growth rates in both periods in `ratio_tb`.
Define the ratio as $r_{20,14}=g_{17,14}/g_{20,14}$.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year,6,7))) - as.numeric(str_sub(birth_date, 1, 4))) |> 
  filter(pre_income >= 4*10^6, 
         age >= 25, age <= 60)

ratio_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = growth) |>  
  filter(is.finite(g_17_14), is.finite(g_20_14)) |>
  mutate(r_20_14 = g_17_14 / g_20_14)

```

## 2 Ratio distributions by threshold

**Share of growth occurring in the first three years**

Exclude observations with ratios exactly equal to zero or one, and set 28 threshold values $u$ from 0.1 to 2.8 in increments of 0.1.
For each threshold, select individuals whose six-year growth satisfies $g_{20,14}>u$.
Restrict the horizontal axis to −0.3–1.3 using `xlim()`.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 6

x_values <- seq(0.1, 2.8, by = 0.1)

plot_tb <- ratio_tb |>
  select(id, r_20_14, g_20_14) |>
  filter(r_20_14 != 0, r_20_14 != 1)

plots <- map(x_values, \(threshold) {
  plot_tb |>
    filter(g_20_14 > threshold) |>
    ggplot(aes(r_20_14)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
    xlim(c(-0.3, 1.3)) +
    ggtitle(paste("u =", threshold)) +
    labs(x = "Ratio", y = "Frequency")
})

walk(plots, print)

walk2(plots, x_values, \(plot, threshold) {
  ggsave(
    filename = str_c("ratio_three_x_", threshold, "_income.png"),
    path = graph_dir,
    plot = plot
  )
})

```
